answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each participant to stake a reputation bond tied to one persistent public key, recorded in a shared atlas of identities. Each new vertex in the trust graph must be endorsed by established agents who risk part of their bond if the newcomer misbehaves. Making many fakes therefore costs real stake, while honest agents build a velvet-smooth record of fulfilled work that cannot be cheaply copied. Sybil floods become uneconomical before they can distort prices or votes.
